title: Vow equivalence ledger
description: Cross-run state for the equivalence-validation tiers. Makes recurring runs incremental (only changed module pairs are re-reviewed) and comparable (a regression is distinguishable from a new finding).

updated.description: ISO-8601 date of the last write. Stamped by the caller, not derived in-process: workflow scripts here must stay deterministic.

pairs.description: Adversarial pair review (tier 3), keyed by pair name e.g. 'lexer'.

rust.description: The Rust side: one or more repo-relative paths, comma-separated. A path may name a directory (e.g. 'vow-syntax/src/parser').

self_hosted.description: The self-hosted side: one or more repo-relative paths, comma-separated.

content_hash.description: sha256 over the contents of every file named by 'rust' and 'self_hosted' — a pair routinely spans several files per side, not one each. A pair whose hash is unchanged since last_reviewed is skipped and reported as skipped — never silently omitted.

outcome.description: clean: reviewed, nothing found. hypotheses: claims raised but none confirmed by the runner. confirmed: at least one runner-confirmed divergence.

confirmed_issues.description: GitHub issue numbers for runner-confirmed divergences.

corpus.description: Per-file divergence history (tier 2), keyed by repo-relative .vow path. Presence here means a file has diverged at least once, so a reappearance is a regression rather than a new finding.

observable.description: The observable(s) this entry documents. reconcile() matches on (file, observable), so a divergence on any observable NOT listed here is reported as new rather than suppressed. Use the array form for a file that legitimately diverges on more than one.

status.description: open: live divergence. fixed: resolved, retained so a reappearance reads as a regression. expected: a known, documented asymmetry (e.g. a diagnostic a phase-shifted checker cannot emit) — must carry a note and an issue.

fixture.description: Repo-relative path of the promoted tier-1 regression fixture, once one exists.

rust_error_codes.description: Exact sorted Rust diagnostic-code multiset for an active error_code divergence.

self_hosted_error_codes.description: Exact sorted self-hosted diagnostic-code multiset for an active error_code divergence.

expected_observables.description: The subset of 'observable' that was reviewed and classified 'expected' before a different observable's divergence forced the entry-wide 'status' to 'open'. Every name here must also appear in 'observable' (enforced by propose_ledger's construction and by the test suite, not by this schema — 2020-12 has no cross-property subset keyword). Purely a review aid: reconcile() suppresses by the entry-wide 'status' alone, so this does not change suppression behavior.

then.description: An 'expected' asymmetry is a standing decision to suppress a finding, so it must carry the rationale and the tracking issue that justify it. Without this the status enum's own prose is unenforced and an entry can bless a divergence silently.

expected_observables only makes sense on a mixed entry that a new, unrelated finding forced to 'open' — the same justification requirement as a whole-entry 'expected' classification applies to the part that was previously reviewed. 'fixed' is also allowed: a full fix retains the entry's fields verbatim as history (mirroring rust_error_codes/self_hosted_error_codes), so a still-open entry that gets entirely fixed in the same sweep keeps its expected_observables too.
An active error-code suppression must pin both exact multisets so a different diagnostic regression cannot inherit the exception.
